name: b1
_comment: B1: reference-derived size classes, measured against the build immediately
before them (bf_pre), inside one campaign.
The ladder changes from 64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096 to
2^k*(BF_MIN_RECORD+sizeof(KVMeta))+sizeof(BfMiniPage), cache-line aligned
(tree.rs:222-250).  A ladder tuned to one record size is NOT a uniform win,
and this config exists to measure that rather than assume it.
Mini-pages hold ~1.2-1.6 records under scrambled zipf, so the class a
SINGLE record lands in is what dominates.  One record costs 24 (header) +
8 (meta) + 8 (rowid key) + value_len.  Falsifiable prediction, per dataset:
dataset  needs   old   new    predicted B/record
v32       72 B   128   128    unchanged
v64      104 B   128   128    unchanged
If v200 does not regress, the model of where the bytes go is wrong and the
B/record column is not measuring what it claims.  That is the real point of
including it: v100 alone would confirm the change and teach nothing.
A 16 MiB ring against 4M rows cycles in seconds, so every cell reaches
steady state well inside the warmup and B/record is a saturated number.
Read B/record and cached recs FIRST; throughput on this shape is expected
to move very little, because the 2026-09-16 warmup sweep showed 20% more
cached records moving the hit rate 35.6% -> 35.0% on the ltm shape, i.e.
capacity is not what binds.  A capacity change should be judged on the
capacity metric.
